PullRequest.Title: git: close the repository of the location a workspace folder left
PullRequest.Body:

**Merge order:** stacked on #348539 (proposed `workspaceFolderLocations` API). Retarget to `main` after it merges.

### What

Cleans up repositories when their workspace folder is removed or switched to another of its locations (for example a git worktree). Worktree auto-detection (`git.detectWorktrees`) is unchanged and may still open other worktrees.

### Changes

- **General behavior change (commit 1, no proposed API):** a removed folder's repository that was kept open for a visible editor now closes once no visible editor uses it. On `main` it stayed open for the rest of the session. This also applies to removing a folder from a multi-root workspace.
- **Commit 1:** added folders are opened after those closures, so a repository nested in a closing one (a worktree inside the primary checkout) is not hidden by its parent.
- **Commit 2:** enables the `workspaceFolderLocations` proposal. When the removed folder's known `locations` include the added folder, it's a switch, and the previous location's repository closes right away, even when it is nested in the new one.
- **Commit 2:** if the locations aren't known yet, the editor swap closes the previous repository. A nested one closes when `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolderLocations` reports it as another location.
- Worktree auto-detection (`git.detectWorktrees`) is unchanged.

### Notes for reviewers

- The decision logic lives in `workspaceFolderRepositories.ts`. `Model` can't be constructed in the integration tests, so the tests drive these classes in `Model`'s order.
- Drive-root folders (`C:\`) are a pre-existing git path-helper limitation, out of scope.

### Validation

- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p extensions/git/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: passed at both commits.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --suite git`: 106 passing, 9 pending, 0 failing on macOS; Windows-gated tests need native Windows CI. They cover drive-letter and path casing, separators, UNC share roots, and the switch, other-location and nested decisions. Their expected values were checked with `path.win32` locally.
- Live in Code OSS (before `locations` became optional), with a file open at each step: primary → wt1 → wt2 → wt1 → primary → nested worktree → primary leaves one repository each time.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A removed workspace folder's repository could survive for the remainder of the session after its last editor closed, retaining repository models, filesystem/.git watchers, and optional periodic fetch activity. Cost accumulated with distinct removed repositories.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Statically evidenced session-long growth in retained repository state/watchers, plus continued status work on filesystem changes and optional network fetches for folders no longer used.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Repositories temporarily kept for visible editors are tracked and disposed when no visible editor belongs to them; re-added workspace repositories are exempted and disposal removes tracker entries.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base workspace-folder handler excludes repositories used by visible editors from disposal at line 483, but its visible-editor handler only detects/opens repositories and never revisits that exclusion. Consequently removing successive folders with an editor open leaves each Repository in Model.openRepositories after its editors disappear. Repository's constructor installs working-tree and .git watchers (repository.ts:932-967), onFileChange schedules status work (3333-3373), and enabled AutoFetcher instances continue periodic git fetch (autofetch.ts:102-136). The added tracker records these repositories (workspaceFolderRepositories.ts:55-56), and model.ts:549-550 disposes them after their last visible editor disappears; the existing disposal path releases repository disposables and removes the model entry. The added test at workspaceFolderRepositories.test.ts:122 exercises this lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate Git and perform the initial workspace scan, including the newly subscribed workspace-folder-locations API.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial Git readiness waits for workspace-folder/editor discovery and directory scanning. openRepository returns after registering a repository; initial status is queued without being awaited. Location resolution starts through the new subscription but is not awaited by Model construction or initial scanning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request workspace-folder locations and push resolved URI/name arrays back to the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One first-listener request per extension-host workspace emitter; each update resolves current folders and sends one response per folder, with stale in-flight resolves cancelled and unchanged location arrays suppressed before events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This Git model did not request or listen for locations; other API subscribers, if present, could already activate the same producer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous, outside Git initial-scan completion; callbacks perform synchronous tracker checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve real paths, discover repository roots with Git subprocesses, and read .git/config when opening new repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Discovery is attempted for candidate paths; exact open-root/real-root checks and repository-root checks prevent duplicate repository construction. Initial workspace scanning and editor detection already performed these operations before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery boundaries existed on the initial scan; there is no new initial per-file or per-history-item Git process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery and trust checks precede repository availability; status runs afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Populate the registered local worktree-location provider's session inventory, if enabled and an agent host has advertised its state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only switchable local single-folder workspaces ask alternate-location providers. At most one provider-store refresh is in flight; a successful listing, including empty success, is retained and updated by notifications. Additional consumers can already have populated it. AgentService also coalesces same-mode in-flight listings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This subscription could not initiate the listing; existing folder pickers/chat worktree consumers could already initiate the same shared provider cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background work; provideLocations returns currently known locations without awaiting this listing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the registered-session catalog and, for ineligible catalog rows, resolve fallback metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bulk catalog read for the host's candidate sessions per actual computation, not one listing per workspace folder. Fallback work is limited to four concurrent resolutions; same-mode concurrent host listings coalesce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing session-list/location consumers reached the same catalog computation; the PR adds a possible initiating consumer rather than changing the catalog algorithm or its limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background to Git activation; needed only when the newly requested provider inventory is not already populated/coalesced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the primary folder's real path for matching session projects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One in-flight/read result per current folder key; successful results are cached and retired with folders. Failed reads are retried on a later ask.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Other location/provider consumers could start this same cached read; Git did not start it through this subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by provideLocations; differing forms cause a subsequent update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F workspace folders, candidate repository paths from the existing scan, and S registered host sessions when the single-folder alternate-location provider is active.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model.openRepository is globally sequentialized, not parallel despite Promise.all. Initial status has a shared limiter of five. Location providers are queried concurrently; there is at most one local provider-store listing in flight and fallback host metadata resolution is limited to four.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exact repository root/real-root checks avoid duplicate models. Provider session listings and real-path forms have shared positive caches; refreshes coalesce. Main-thread resolutions cancel superseded work and extension-host location events suppress equal arrays. Failed inventory/path reads can retry on later asks.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the traced asynchronous boundaries, cache sharing, and single-folder/provider restrictions; no evidence of a newly unbounded process burst or a new wait on Git readiness.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing or profile data. The additional background inventory work depends on worktree-feature enablement, advertised agent state, existing consumers, catalog eligibility, and history size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence reportable regression. The subscription adds bounded background metadata initialization, but it does not place session listing on Git's readiness critical path or multiply backend listings by folder/session count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add workspace folders or switch to another repository/worktree, including a worktree nested in the closing repository.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Compute closures synchronously, dispose selected repositories, then choose added folders and await their queued openRepository discovery. Git SCM availability for the destination waits for the discovery queue, not its initial status.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Git root and .git discovery for added folders not equal to an already open root or real root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One openRepository attempt per eligible added folder, globally serialized. A candidate subdirectory of an already open repository now receives discovery; if it resolves to the same repository, the second exact-root check returns before model creation. Distinct nested repositories are opened once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The ancestor-based getOpenRepository filter skipped every added descendant of an open repository, including distinct nested worktrees. Other eligible additions already used the same Git discovery calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery is awaited by the workspace-folder handler and precedes destination repository registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve candidate and repository real paths and read Git config on genuine opens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Candidate-path realpath can occur even when the candidate ultimately resolves to an open ancestor. Config/model setup occurs only after the discovered root is confirmed not open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Added descendants skipped by the old filter did not perform these discovery reads; actual eligible opens already did.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of serialized repository discovery; no synchronous filesystem API was introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove old SCM/watch registrations and register destination SCM/watch state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One disposal per deduplicated repository returned by the tracker; one setup per genuinely new repository. Existing worktree/submodule autodetection remains separately capped by its configured limits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same setup/cleanup APIs were used, but old-location repositories could remain open and nested destinations could be skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local disposal precedes destination selection; remote registration/disposal messages follow the existing APIs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A added folders, R currently open repositories, and actual distinct repository roots after discovery; location comparisons additionally depend on removed-folder location counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Global openRepository sequencer; status work remains capped at five. Closures are synchronous and deduplicated with a Set.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new added-folder filter checks open root and real-root equality. openRepository independently checks the candidate and then the discovered root, preserving deduplication. No new persistent discovery cache or negative-cache retry loop was added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the before/after boundary count and actual serialization; no evidence of repeated discovery beyond each newly eligible added candidate.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Discovery latency depends on filesystem/Git performance and the number of additions. Additional discovery for descendants is statically established but necessary to distinguish nested repositories under the behavior introduced by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable high-confidence regression: the added boundary calls implement nested-repository discovery, while duplicate model creation and concurrent status bursts remain bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remove a workspace folder while one of its editors is visible, then close/switch its last visible editor or re-add the folder.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor-change handling first resolves visible-editor repository membership and checks retained repositories, disposing those no longer used. Existing editor-based auto-detection then runs if enabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Release SCM registrations, filesystem watchers, listeners, and optional AutoFetcher activity for no-longer-used repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Each retained OpenRepository is removed from the tracker before being returned for disposal; disposal also deletes tracker entries. Re-adding its containing workspace folder forgets retention instead of disposing it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A repository excluded from removal-time cleanup because an editor was visible stayed open after that editor disappeared, retaining watchers and optional periodic fetch activity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Disposal is initiated before editor-based discovery continues; no new Git process or network request is performed by tracker membership checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing background status refresh and configured periodic Git fetch for retained repositories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously continued per unused repository for the remaining session; after cleanup, future watcher-driven work and autofetch loops stop. File-change work is debounced/throttled; autofetch is optional.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unused removed repositories remained eligible for this background I/O indefinitely.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background activity, not an added editor-change wait.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: E visible editors, R open repositories, T temporarily retained repositories, and F current workspace folders. New membership work is bounded by these current collections; no history of disposed repositories is kept.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Membership resolution/disposal is synchronous. Existing getOpenRepository sorting is reused; any later repository discovery is globally sequentialized. Existing status debouncing/throttling and optional fetch scheduling are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The retained Set holds repository identities only while required. Disposal and re-addition remove identities; existing open-root checks prevent re-creation for already-covered editors.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the old path retained live repository resources after last-editor disappearance and that the new disposal path releases them.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Retained model sizes, filesystem activity, and autofetch enablement vary. No measurements were made.
Scenarios.Verdict: This fixes a concrete cleanup/retention performance regression rather than introducing one. Recorded through report_regression_fix with base-line blame provenance.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve previously unknown workspace-folder locations after switching away from a nested worktree.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A location event checks only repositories recorded as kept inside remaining workspace folders, removes matched identities, and initiates their disposal. This event is asynchronous to the initial folder switch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deliver changed location metadata and dispose repositories proven to be old locations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One response per current folder resolution; unchanged arrays do not fire extension-host change events. Each matched kept repository is deleted before it is returned for closure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Git did not react to location updates, so nested old-location repositories remained open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No awaited filesystem, Git, database, or network read is added by the Model event handler; it consumes already delivered metadata.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K kept-in-workspace repository identities, F workspace folders, and L known locations per folder; comparisons are O(K*F*L), with matched repositories removed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local comparisons and disposal initiation; provider resolution scheduling remains outside this handler.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: keptInWorkspace is bounded by still-open repository identities, explicitly cleared on disposal, and matched entries are removed after closure. Location-provider positive caches and update coalescing are described in the activation scenario.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in collection bounds and absence of expensive reads inside the added consumer callback.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large K/F/L combinations are not measured; no retained history or independently increasing key set was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. The added callback closes old live resources and does not create per-location subprocess or network fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ordinary visible-editor changes after startup, with no removed repositories awaiting cleanup.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new prelude constructs visible repository membership, then the unchanged trust/configuration checks and editor auto-detection proceed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible editor count E and current open repository count R; getRepository reuses the existing in-memory lookup/sort. Both new tracker Sets are empty in this scenario.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous in-memory membership calculation. Any existing editor discovery remains subject to Model's global openRepository sequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new repository discovery is triggered by the prelude; ordinary editor detection retains existing root checks. Empty tracker Sets retain no historical repository objects.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the added work is in-memory and performs no subprocess/IPC/filesystem/database/network calls in this empty-tracker path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extra CPU/allocation depends on visible split count and open repositories; no evidence establishes a substantial user-visible regression from this bounded additional lookup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable high-confidence regression; the additional membership pass alone does not establish a meaningful performance bug.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the entire six-file changed inventory and every diff page in one performance-review pass. Traced folder/editor/location lifecycle ownership, Git discovery serialization, status limits, provider-cache behavior, and transitive location IPC/catalog reads. No new high-confidence actionable performance findings. Recorded one concrete removed-folder repository-retention fix and its base-blame provenance. Review is static; no profiling or runtime execution.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
